Accounts.reason: Records carry their company; so the contract must only return stored records.

content.statement: Users are accounts of a company, records are contacts and deals, and sharing is a table of shares.
content.why: A record belongs to the company stored on it, and a user to the company of their account. This trusts the record, so ReadContract requires returned records to be the stored ones; it also trusts the account, which authentication provides (not modelled).
substitutions: sharedWith := (r: CrmRecord, t: TenantId) => shares.value.contains(Share(r.id, t))

ReadApi.reason: Users only see records through searches; revisit if we add exports.

content.statement: Records are shown only as query results, and a query returns only records the user may see.
content.why: Users find records by searching, so what a user sees is what their queries return. abs: a user is shown a record when some query of theirs returns it.

sources.spec: run => forall((u: User.T, q: Query.T) => run(u, q).forall(r => visible(u, r)))
sources.abs: run => (u, r) => exists((q: Query.T) => run(u, q).contains(r))

User: a person who works for a company
owner: the company a record belongs to
sharedWith: whether the record's company shared it with the given company
tenantOf: the company a user works for
uses: fun (u : User) (r : Record) => (((owner r) = (tenantOf u)) ∨ (sharedWith r (tenantOf u)))

ReadContract.reason: Returns only stored, matching records the user may see. It does not promise to return all of them; that is listed as not modelled.

content.statement: A search returns only stored records that match it, each of the user's company or shared with it.
content.why: Accounts, stated for one call, plus what a search asks for. A returned record must be one of the stored records, so an implementation cannot relabel another company's record as the user's.

sources.post: (user, query, result) => result.forall(r => store.value.contains(r) && matches(query, r) && (r.tenant == user.tenant || shares.value.contains(Share(r.id, user.tenant))))

examples: expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), Everything) ⇒ List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"))  given store = List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact")), shares = List()  — Ann lists everything she can see: Acme's deal

expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), ById(2)) ⇒ List()  given store = List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact")), shares = List()  — Globex's contact is not shared with Acme

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), ById(2)) ⇒ List(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"))  given store = List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact")), shares = List()  — another company's record is never returned

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), Everything) ⇒ List(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("acme"), Contact, "Globex contact"))  given store = List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact")), shares = List()  — a record relabelled as Acme's is not a stored record

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), OfKind(Contact)) ⇒ List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"))  given store = List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact")), shares = List()  — a search for contacts does not return deals

expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), OfKind(Contact)) ⇒ List(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"))  given store = List(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact")), shares = List(Share(2, TenantId("acme")))  — Globex shared its contact with Acme, so Ann finds it by kind
vocabulary: shares: the share table as stored when the search runs
store: the records as stored when the search runs; a record id is unique across all companies
uses:
structure Account where
  email : String
  tenant : TenantId

inductive Search where
  | ById (id : Int)
  | OfKind (kind : Kind)
  | Everything

structure CrmRecord where
  id : Int
  tenant : TenantId
  kind : Kind
  title : String

structure Share where
  record : Int
  to : TenantId
fun (q : Search) (r : CrmRecord) => (match q with | Search.ById id => (r.id = id) | Search.OfKind k => (r.kind = k) | Search.Everything => True)

content.why: Isolation between companies is what the idea says must hold. Companies, users, records and sharing are left open.

content.idea:
# CRM

Many companies use one CRM. Each company's users manage contacts and deals.
A user may see a record only if it belongs to their company, or if the record's
company has shared it with theirs. Users find records by id, by kind, or list
everything they can see.
content.notModelled:
- Who may create or remove a share.
- That the account a search runs for is the caller's own (authentication).
- That a search returns every matching record the user may see: only what it
  must not return is modelled.
- Writing records.
